description: A four-panel figure of Charpy impact load–deflection curves measured on a Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si low-density steel at three testing temperatures. Panels (a), (b) and (c) share identical axes: Charpy impact load (kN), 0–35, versus Deflection (mm), 0–25+. Each plot contains a black "Experimental curve" and a red "ISO-evaluation curve" (legend at top right), with a colour-coded legend for the energy partitions W_initiation (light pink), W_stable (orange), W_unstable (brown) and W_collapse (white). (a) is −196 °C: peak load ≈32 kN at ~4 mm deflection, curve terminates near 10 mm, "Crack initiation point" arrow, label Fm(Fin), and RC=10.9957. (b) is −77 °C: peak ≈27 kN near 5 mm, curve ends near 20 mm, RC=4.6215. (c) is RT: peak ≈24 kN near 5–6 mm, curve extended to ~25 mm, RC=3.7864. In all three, loads Fgy, Fin, Fm, Fiu, Fa are marked and vertical dashed lines bound the four shaded energy regions. (d) plots the characteristic values Fgy (squares), Fm (circles) and Fin (triangles) against Temperature (°C), −200 to 50, on the left Load (kN) axis (15–35), together with Fiu/Fm (red triangles) on the right axis (0.5–1.0). The figure demonstrates that Fgy, Fm, Fin and Fiu/Fm all rise as temperature falls, while Fiu/Fm approaches 1 at −196 °C, i.e. the steel carries larger impact loads and initiates cracks with more difficulty at cryogenic temperature.

observations.observation: Panels (a)-(c) are load–deflection curves with identical axes: Charpy impact load (kN) 0–35 versus Deflection (mm) 0–25, each overlaying a black 'Experimental curve' and a red 'ISO-evaluation curve'.
The printed rebound-compliance values are RC=10.9957 in (a), RC=4.6215 in (b) and RC=3.7864 in (c), i.e. RC decreases as testing temperature rises.
Panel (a) reaches the highest peak load (about 32 kN) and the shortest total deflection (curve ends near 10 mm), while panel (c) has the lowest peak (about 24 kN) and the longest tail (to ~25 mm).
In panel (a) the peak load is annotated 'Fm(Fin)', indicating Fm and Fin coincide at −196 °C, whereas in (b) and (c) Fin and Fm are marked separately with Fin below Fm.
Each of panels (a)-(c) shades four regions labelled W_initiation, W_stable, W_unstable and W_collapse, separated by vertical dashed lines at the loads Fgy, Fin, Fiu and Fa.
An arrow labelled 'Crack initiation point' marks the deviation of the experimental curve from the ISO-evaluation curve in panels (a), (b) and (c).
In panel (d), Fgy, Fm and Fin (left Load axis, 15–35 kN) all decrease as temperature increases, and Fiu/Fm (right axis, 0.5–1.0) shows the same negative temperature dependence.
Fiu/Fm is highest (close to 0.98) at the lowest temperature near −196 °C and lowest (about 0.83) at the highest temperature near 25 °C.

The caption identifies the panels as smoothed impact load–deflection curves at (a) −196 °C, (b) −77 °C and (c) RT, with (d) giving the corresponding characteristic values changing with testing temperature.
The citing text states Fgy is the transition load from elastic to plastic deformation and Fm is the maximum Charpy impact load at the peak of the curve.
The citing text states that at −196 °C Fin is almost equal to Fm because the compliance-changing-rate curve shows no obvious slope change.
The citing text reports W_initiation values of 112, 68 and 57 J at −196 °C, −77 °C and RT respectively; these numbers are not printed in the figure itself.
The citing text defines rebound compliance (RC) as the absolute slope of the curve from Fiu to Fa and notes that a larger RC at lower temperature indicates more rapid unstable crack propagation.
The citing text interprets the larger Fiu/Fm at lower temperature as cracks propagating rapidly from the stable to the unstable regime.

subfigures.description: Charpy load–deflection curve at −196 °C; black experimental and red ISO-evaluation curves peak near 32 kN at ~4 mm deflection and end near 10 mm. Fgy, Fin, Fm (labelled 'Fm(Fin)'), Fiu and Fa are marked, the four absorbed-energy regions W_initiation/W_stable/W_unstable/W_collapse are shaded, and RC=10.9957 is printed; an arrow points to the 'Crack initiation point'.

Charpy load–deflection curve at −77 °C; peak load ~27 kN near 5 mm deflection, curve tail extending to ~20 mm. Fgy, Fin, Fm, Fiu, Fa marked, the same four shaded energy regions and RC=4.6215 labelled, with the 'Crack initiation point' arrow.

Charpy load–deflection curve at RT; peak load ~24 kN near 5–6 mm deflection with a long tail to ~25 mm. Fgy, Fin, Fm, Fiu, Fa marked, four shaded energy partitions, RC=3.7864 printed, and the 'Crack initiation point' arrow.

Line plot of characteristic impact values versus testing temperature from about −196 °C to +25 °C: Fgy (squares), Fm (circles) and Fin (triangles) on the left Load (kN) axis (15–35), and Fiu/Fm (red triangles) on the right axis (0.5–1.0). All four quantities decrease monotonically with increasing temperature, Fgy from ~22 to ~17 kN, Fm from ~32 to ~24.5 kN, Fin from ~31.5 to ~22.5 kN, and Fiu/Fm from ~0.98 to ~0.83.

unreadable_items: Panel (d): numerical tick labels on both y-axes are small; values quoted for Fgy, Fm, Fin and Fiu/Fm are read from marker positions between gridlines and are approximate
Panel (b) and (c): some dotted/dashed evaluation-curve detail and the exact x-position of the vertical boundary lines cannot be resolved precisely
